repositories.label: Service Index Django
questions: Do the viewer/editor boundaries consistently protect browser views, exports, logs, staff/contact data, event workflows, and the API?
Does the hosts API retain its authenticated GET-only contract, group authorization, explicit response fields, and safe exposure of host/contact fields?
Do CILogon/allauth signup and login policies, and the access_django_user_admin producer/consumer interface, remain intentional and fail-closed?
Do route decorators and method checks protect legacy login/logout/lock cleanup and username-based privilege helpers, and do validation/logging/tests protect inventory and contact data?
Are schema or migration changes compatible with documented multi-schema procedures and existing database consumers?
Do dependency recommendations compare the local uv environment with the infrastructure-selected production uv project and lock, without copying transient pins?
Which proposed changes affect auth, API schema, exports, personal/host data, migrations, or external package interfaces and need an explicit plan?

repositories.label: Service Index Infrastructure
questions: Do Terraform provider/backend/resource patterns follow current least-privilege, encryption, network exposure, and state-handling practices?
Do Ansible roles, inventory boundaries, privilege escalation, idempotency, and secret references follow current safe patterns?
Are deployment inputs and application release selection traceable to their sources of truth without hardcoded environment details?
What Ubuntu LTS release and support window do the managed hosts use, and are standard apt security updates, routine package upgrades, and required reboots handled consistently?
Is Ubuntu 24.04 still the right destination, or should the currently supported LTS target also be compared for support runway and compatibility?

If considering Ubuntu 22.04 to 24.04, do the infrastructure-declared app dependencies, packages, services, configuration, and host image remain compatible; what release-note or package-source changes need attention?

Does the infrastructure code support a parallel host/image rebuild or an in-place release upgrade, and has the chosen approach included backup/restore, maintenance window, reboot, rollback, and post-upgrade service checks in a human-reviewed plan?
Are host hardening, patching, TLS, backups, monitoring, and recovery documented with evidence?
Which recommendations require Terraform or Ansible validation that the reviewer is prohibited from running?

repositories.label: Portal CMS Django
questions: Does APP_CONFIG remain the required, validated runtime-config entry point without exposing its contents or weakening production settings?
Do CILogon login/signup rules remain distinct from Resource Provider membership ownership, with page/news/resource permissions fail-closed?
Do CMS draft/review/publish locks, focus-area editor/publisher roles, and POST-only state transitions preserve the intended workflow?
Do public news feeds preserve published/active filtering, route and serialized-field contracts, cache behavior, and consumer compatibility?
Do CIDER resource views and sync preserve upstream validation, caching/fallback rules, transaction semantics, dry-run behavior, and guarded stale-group pruning?
Does healthz expose only intended readiness/version information and keep database failure details generic?
Are test commands separated from database-mutating integration scripts, and is every requested check restricted to deliberately nonproduction config?
Do dependency recommendations compare the app manifest with the infrastructure-selected uv project and lock, without copying transient pins?
Which proposed changes affect auth/group ownership, page workflow, public feeds, CIDER data, migrations, or external schemas and need an explicit plan?

repositories.label: Portal CMS Infrastructure
questions: Do Terraform resources and backends use least privilege, encryption, narrow network exposure, and safe state practices?
Do Ansible deployment tasks use safe secret references, explicit targeting, idempotent configuration, and bounded privilege?
What Ubuntu LTS release and support window do the managed hosts use, and are standard apt security updates, routine package upgrades, and required reboots handled consistently?
Is Ubuntu 24.04 still the right destination, or should the currently supported LTS target also be compared for support runway and compatibility?

If considering Ubuntu 22.04 to 24.04, do the infrastructure-declared app dependencies, packages, services, configuration, and host image remain compatible; what release-note or package-source changes need attention?

Does the infrastructure code support a parallel host/image rebuild or an in-place release upgrade, and has the chosen approach included backup/restore, maintenance window, reboot, rollback, and post-upgrade service checks in a human-reviewed plan?
Are migration enablement, static collection, and service restart behavior clearly separated and controlled?
Are Nginx, Gunicorn, PostgreSQL connectivity, TLS/certificate handling, patching, backups, and monitoring aligned with current practices?
Which follow-up validations are explicitly forbidden to the reviewer and must remain pending for an authorized operator?
